response.title: how long will a solar generator power your house
response.answer:
A solar generator can power your house for anywhere from a few hours to several days, depending on the battery capacity, how much electricity your house uses, and whether solar panels can recharge it.

The biggest difference is whether you're powering your entire house or just essential appliances.

How long different solar generators last

Assuming the batteries start fully charged, with no additional solar charging:

Estimates assume 85% usable energy after conversion losses. Actual runtime varies with appliance use and system efficiency.
What can you power?

Small portable solar generator (2–5 kWh)

Runs a refrigerator, Wi-Fi, lights, and phone chargers for several hours to roughly a day, depending on usage.

Shop

Large solar generator (10–20 kWh)

Can keep essential appliances running for 1–2+ days, or support heavier household loads for shorter periods.

Shop

Whole-home solar battery system (30–50+ kWh)

Can support a substantial portion of household electricity use, especially when paired with rooftop solar panels.

What if you have solar panels?

Solar panels can extend the runtime significantly. For example, a 20 kWh battery paired with 5 kW of solar panels might generate approximately 15–25 kWh on a reasonably sunny day, depending on location, season, and system losses.

If your house uses 15 kWh per day, that could be enough to replenish the electricity you consume and potentially keep you powered through multiple days of good weather.

markup:
A **solar generator can power your house for anywhere from a few hours to several days**, depending on the battery capacity, how much electricity your house uses, and whether solar panels can recharge it.

The biggest difference is whether you're powering your **entire house** or just essential appliances.

## How long different solar generators last

Assuming the batteries start fully charged, with no additional solar charging:

| Battery capacity | Essential appliances (300W) | Whole-house load (2,000W) |
|---|---|---|
| 2 kWh | 5–6 hours | ~50 minutes |
| 5 kWh | 14 hours | ~2 hours |
| 10 kWh | 28 hours | ~4 hours |
| 20 kWh | 2.3 days | ~8 hours |
| 30 kWh | 3.5 days | ~13 hours |
| 50 kWh | 5.9 days | ~21 hours |

<caption>Estimates assume 85% usable energy after conversion losses. Actual runtime varies with appliance use and system efficiency.</caption>

## What can you power?

<box gap={3}>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="portable solar power station battery with folding solar panels backyard" aspectRatio="5:4" maxWidth="144px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Small portable solar generator (2–5 kWh)**

      Runs a refrigerator, Wi-Fi, lights, and phone chargers for several hours to roughly a day, depending on usage.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="large home backup battery power station modular EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra installation" aspectRatio="5:4" maxWidth="144px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Large solar generator (10–20 kWh)**

      Can keep essential appliances running for 1–2+ days, or support heavier household loads for shorter periods.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="residential solar panels roof with wall mounted home battery energy storage system" aspectRatio="5:4" maxWidth="144px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Whole-home solar battery system (30–50+ kWh)**

      Can support a substantial portion of household electricity use, especially when paired with rooftop solar panels.
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## What if you have solar panels?

Solar panels can extend the runtime significantly. For example, a 20 kWh battery paired with 5 kW of solar panels might generate approximately 15–25 kWh on a reasonably sunny day, depending on location, season, and system losses.

If your house uses 15 kWh per day, that could be enough to replenish the electricity you consume and potentially keep you powered through multiple days of good weather.

## Calculate your home's runtime

{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState(20)}
{@body const [daily,setDaily] = DIL.useState(20)}
{@body const usable = capacity*0.85}
{@body const runtime = usable/daily}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      **Battery capacity**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{capacity} kWh</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={2} max={60} step={1} value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}/>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      **Daily electricity consumption**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{daily} kWh/day</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={5} max={80} step={1} value={daily} onChange={setDaily}/>
  </box>
  <box background="surface-secondary" padding={3} radius="lg" align="center" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated runtime without sunlight</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{runtime >= 2 ? `${runtime.toFixed(1)} days` : `${(runtime*24).toFixed(1)} hours`}</title>
    <caption>85% usable capacity assumed</caption>
  </box>
</box>

**One question:** Are you trying to power your entire house, including air conditioning, or just essential appliances during a power outage?

That makes a huge difference in how large a solar generator you'll need.
